text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
Former New South Wales Premier SIR ROBERT ASKIN was born in 1909.
American blues singer MUDDY WATERS, whose hits included "I've Got My Mojo Working" and "Mannish Boy", was born in 1915.
American poet, playwright and novelist MAYA ANGELOU was born in 1928.
UK guitarist with 'Slade' DAVE HILL was born in 1952. The band was successful in the seventies and then again in the mid eighties.
UK singer JULIE FORSYTH was born in 1958. She was a member of "Guys n' Dolls", who had hits with "There's A Whole Lot Of Loving" (1975) and "You Don't Have To Say You Love Me" (1976).
** EVENTS **
1581 : QUEEN ELIZABETH knighted FRANCIS DRAKE aboard the

celebrated vessel "PELICAN" (later renamed "GOLDEN HIND"), in which he had circumnavigated the globe. The ship was later broken up, and a chair made out of the relics was presented to the University of Oxford, where it now stands in the Bodleian Library.
1849 : Prussia's FREDERICK WILLIAM IV was elected Emperor
of Germany, but refused to take the crown.
1896 : Gold was discovered in the Yukon in the North West
of Canada.
1900 : A 16 year-old boy attempted to kill the heir to
the throne of England, PRINCE EDWARD, firing 2 shots at him as the PRINCE and PRINCESS ALEXANDRA were sitting in a train at a Brussels railway station.
1949 : Britain, Canada, the United States, France,
Belgium, Holland, Luxembourg, Norway, Denmark, Iceland, Italy and Portugal signed the "North Atlantic Treaty" to protect Western Nations from possible Soviet aggression.
1955 : The Australian government revealed the new atomic
testing site in South Australia was to be called Maralinga, which was Aboriginal for thunder. Britain exploded an atomic device at the site on the 29th September 1956.
1963 : The BEATLES took the first 5 places on the United
States 'singles'charts with "Can't Buy Me Love", "Twist And Shout", "She Loves You", I Want To Hold Your Hand" and "Please Please Me".
1968 : American civil rights leader MARTIN LUTHER KING

was shot dead at a motel in Memphis. The son of a preacher, KING became famous around the globe in 1963 with his "I Have A Dream" speech, and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1964. One of his other famous quotes was "If a man hasn't discovered something he would die for, he isn't fit to live".
1979 : Australia's first international air hijack attempt
ended with police shooting the would-be hijacker at Sydney airport. A woman hostage and a policeman were stabbed after the hijacker demanded to be flown to Moscow via Singapore and Rome.
1979 : More than three thousand truck drivers staged
blockades in four states - Queensland, New South Wales, Victoria and South Australia. They were demanding the abolition of road taxes.
1979 : Ousted Pakistani Prime Minister ZULFIKAR ALI
BHUTTO was hanged by the new military regime for the alleged murder of a political opponent.
1981 : The Brixton area of South London became a battle
zone, as 200 Police were wounded in running riots with youths.
1984 : World media attention focused on New Zealand,
where it was claimed that a man had beaten his wife to death with a frozen sausage!
1986 : Media mogul RUPERT MURDOCH offered to make peace
with striking workers at his newspaper factory at Wapping, by giving-up another plant to the Printers' Union.
